# Thaıdene Nëné National Park Reserve

Thaıdene Nëné - “The Land of the Ancestors” in Dënesųłiné Yati – is an Indigenous Protected Area of more than 26 000 km2 in the Northwest Territories. At its core is Thaıdene Nëné National Park Reserve. Here is the place where the barrens and subarctic boreal forest converge on the shore of one of the world’s largest freshwater lakes in a stunning display of rugged, northern beauty.

Management of Thaıdene Nëné National Park Reserve is shared with the Indigenous governments who have a cultural connection to the landscape: Łutsël K’é Dene First Nation, Northwest Territory Métis Nation, Deninu Kųę First Nation, and Yellowknives Dene First Nation. This is a culturally rich and spiritually significant area, where the continued relationship between the land and Indigenous people highlights the importance of protected areas.

![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/pn-np/nt/woodbuffalo/2024-changes/01_11-nodrone/No-Drone_nobkgd.png)
Using recreational drones in Thaıdene Nëné National Park Reserve is prohibited. Operating a drone within park boundaries may face law enforcement action and a fine of up to $25,000.

## More places to discover with Parks Canada

[![Tehjeh Deé ](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/WET4/proximite-nearby/nwt/nattsihchoh-640x360.jpg?modified=20221126220102)](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nt/naatsihchoh)

### [Nááts'įhch'oh National Park Reserve](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nt/naatsihchoh)

In the headwaters of Tehjeh Deé (South Nahanni River) Nááts'įhch'oh National Park Reserve is a place where culture and nature are intertwined. Nááts'įhch'oh offers whitewater paddling and off-the-grid hiking in the Northwest Territories for experienced adventurers.

[![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/WET4/proximite-nearby/nwt/nahanni-640x360.jpg?modified=20221126220102)](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nt/nahanni)

### [Nahanni National Park Reserve](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nt/nahanni)

Remote granite pinnacles lure top alpinists, wilderness river tripping opportunities attract paddlers, interpreters share cultural and natural history with river trippers, campers and day flight visitors.

[![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/WET4/proximite-nearby/nwt/wood-buffalo-640x360.jpg?modified=20221126220102)](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nt/woodbuffalo)

### [Wood Buffalo National Park](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nt/woodbuffalo)

Wood Buffalo National Park is our country's largest national park and one of the largest in the world. It protects an outstanding and representative example of Canada's Northern Boreal Plains.

# Safety and guidelines

## Thaıdene Nëné National Park Reserve

### [Bear safety](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nt/thaidene-nene/security-safety/ours-bears)

Bear safety, prevention, wildlife encounters, camping, deterrents, and reporting.

### [Backcountry safety](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nt/thaidene-nene/security-safety/backcountry)

Trip planning, emergencies, weather hazards, wildlife safety, and backcountry travel.

### [Fire bans & restrictions - FAQ](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nt/thaidene-nene/security-safety/feu-qfp-faq-fire)

Fire regulations, permitted activities, wildfire prevention, restrictions, and safety information.

### [Boating and paddling safety](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nt/thaidene-nene/security-safety/nautisme-boating)

Water safety, trip planning, weather conditions, cold-water risks, equipment, and navigation.

### [Muskox safety](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nt/thaidene-nene/security-safety/muskox)

Wildlife safety, viewing distances, animal behaviour, encounter guidance, and visitor precautions.

### [Winter safety](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nt/thaidene-nene/security-safety/hiver-winter)

Winter travel hazards, emergency preparedness, hypothermia prevention, frostbite, and trip planning.

Snowmobile travel, ice conditions, trip planning, essential equipment, and safe riding practices.

### [Communications](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nt/thaidene-nene/security-safety/comms)

Emergency communications, satellite phones, locator beacons, safety planning, and emergency contacts.

### [Important bulletins](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nt/thaidene-nene/security-safety/bulletins)

Current advisories, closures, restrictions, superintendent’s orders, and visitor notices.

You are responsible for your own safety while travelling in Thaıdene Nëné National Park Reserve. It is important to be prepared and well-informed before setting off on an adventure, so that you can minimize your risk if something unexpected happens. [Registering](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nt/thaidene-nene/visit/inscription-registration) your trip is a critical part of the planning process and provides Parks Canada with critical information in the event that an emergency response is required.

At Parks Canada, we do our part to help reduce your risk by assessing and managing hazards and making sure that up-to-date safety information is available. The information on this website can help you plan, but if you need more support please do not hesitate to contact our office directly and our staff will provide you with the most recent conditions and guidance available.

Being fully prepared will help to ensure that your visit to this special place is safe, enjoyable and memorable.

For important information about staying safe while enjoying Thaıdene Nëné National Park Reserve, please explore the topics below.

[![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/pn-np/nt/thaidene-nene/securite-safety/bear-with-cubs260x140.jpg?h=140&w=260&hash=A9240A50C8899898738E81FA31BCEDC0)](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nt/thaidene-nene/security-safety/ours-bears "bear country")[Safe travel in bear country](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nt/thaidene-nene/security-safety/ours-bears "bear country") Thaıdene Nëné is home to both grizzly and black bears. Familiarize yourself with the principles and practices of safe travel in bear country.

[![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/pn-np/nt/thaidene-nene/securite-safety/Open-Country-along-the-Snowdrift-River_260-140.jpg?h=140&w=260&hash=A4B35BD9A2A14458FAE036D01DC4F677)](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nt/thaidene-nene/security-safety/backcountry "backcountry security")[backcountry security](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nt/thaidene-nene/security-safety/backcountry "backcountry security") [Backcountry safety](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nt/thaidene-nene/security-safety/backcountry "backcountry security")Thaıdene Nëné is a remote wilderness park. Travellers must be self-sufficient and able to handle emergency situations on their own. Plan ahead and ensure that you are properly equipped for your trip.

[![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/pn-np/nt/thaidene-nene/securite-safety/winter-skidoos-and-sunset_260x140.jpg?h=140&w=260&hash=113C4178CF1E5FB3087F7F9F694C0497)Winter safety](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nt/thaidene-nene/security-safety/hiver-winter "Winter Security") Thaıdene Nëné is a winter wonderland with cross country skiing, ice fishing, snowshoeing, dog sledding, backcountry camping and snowmobiling fun for all! To ensure you have a safe and enjoyable trip, please be prepared!

**To report an emergency** within the National Park Reserve, contact: 1-780-852-3100
